title: Memory doesn't make an agent; orchestration does.
text: A model that remembers its session is still a function call. An agent keeps running, decides what to do next and coordinates its own work.

title: Give agents simple tools and let them build the rest.
text: You can't hand-write every tool an agent will need. Plain shell access and the freedom to write its own tools go further than a long list of integrations.

title: An agent will never tell you no.
text: It will open the pull request and write the 3,000 lines. The checks have to come from you: your own review, guards in the repo, and limits on what its credentials can reach.

title: Contribute with an agent the way a person would.
text: One idea per pull request, polish before you publish, and reply to maintainers yourself.

title: Voice agents are cheap enough for real errands.
text: Booking a restaurant table by phone costs under 20 cents a call, and the agent gets better by reading its own call transcripts.
